A deep dive into building robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines using LangChain, vector databases, and FastAPI for production AI applications.

Building Production RAG Pipelines with LangChain

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the go-to architecture for building AI applications that need to work with your own data. In this post, I'll walk through how I built a production RAG system that handles thousands of queries daily.

The Problem

Large Language Models are powerful, but they have a critical limitation — their knowledge is frozen at training time. For real-world applications, you need your AI to work with current, private, or domain-specific data.

RAG solves this by retrieving relevant context from your data store before generating a response.

Architecture Overview

from langchain.vectorstores import Chroma
from langchain.embeddings import OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.chains import RetrievalQA

# 1. Embed your documents
embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings()
vectorstore = Chroma.from_documents(
    documents=docs,
    embedding=embeddings,
    persist_directory="./chroma_db"
)

# 2. Build retrieval chain
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4", temperature=0)
qa_chain = RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(
    llm=llm,
    retriever=vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 5}),
    return_source_documents=True,
)

# 3. Query
result = qa_chain({"query": "What is the disaster response protocol?"})
print(result["result"])

Key Production Considerations

1. Chunking Strategy

How you split documents dramatically affects retrieval quality:

from langchain.text_splitter import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter

splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=512,
    chunk_overlap=64,
    separators=["\n\n", "\n", ".", " "],
)
chunks = splitter.split_documents(raw_docs)

2. Hybrid Search

Pure semantic search misses exact keyword matches. Combine both:

from langchain.retrievers import BM25Retriever, EnsembleRetriever

semantic = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 5})
keyword = BM25Retriever.from_documents(docs, k=5)

hybrid = EnsembleRetriever(
    retrievers=[keyword, semantic],
    weights=[0.4, 0.6]
)

3. Re-ranking

After retrieval, re-rank results using a cross-encoder for better relevance:

from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder

reranker = CrossEncoder("cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2")

def rerank(query, docs, top_k=3):
    pairs = [(query, doc.page_content) for doc in docs]
    scores = reranker.predict(pairs)
    ranked = sorted(zip(scores, docs), reverse=True)
    return [doc for _, doc in ranked[:top_k]]

Results

After implementing these optimizations on my Disaster Response AI Copilot:

  • Retrieval accuracy: 73% → 91%
  • Response latency: 3.2s → 1.1s
  • Hallucination rate: 18% → 4%

Conclusion

Production RAG is not just about plugging in LangChain — it requires careful attention to chunking, retrieval strategy, and re-ranking. The reward is an AI system that's both accurate and up-to-date.
